title: Power board ANOVA_PRO_POWER_REV01 - bottom side
source: FCC ID 2APBOAN600, internal-photos exhibit 3999178 (2018 sample), page 3, bottom photo (991x371); flipped top-to-bottom vs. power_top

callouts.label: 30-pin FPC connector to main board
callouts.note: Ribbon to main board J8. The interface pinout between the boards is a key Phase 1 task.

callouts.label: Test points beside the FPC
callouts.note: Convenient probing of rails and signals entering from the main board.

callouts.label: DC/DC buck inductor 6.8 uH
callouts.note: Part of a switching regulator with output caps C17/C31. Probably makes the supply for J8, which the main board expects at about 5 V (its 3.3 V LDO U17 takes at most 6 V; J-076), or a rail for this board itself (guess).

callouts.label: IC, unidentified (pins on two sides)
callouts.note: Biggest IC on the power board. Candidates: buck controller, power-board MCU, or sensor AFE. If it is an MCU, it has firmware too, which matters for the update-failure analysis.

callouts.label: 6-lead SOP IC + power resistors (20 R, 51 R)
callouts.part: SOP-8 body with 6 leads; resistors marked '200' and '510'
callouts.note: Under the AC/DC module area. Missing pins suggest a high-voltage part: offline regulator, triac/MOSFET driver or opto. MAINS POTENTIAL.

callouts.label: Test point at the root of the sensor finger
Sensor-finger tip: component footprint
callouts.note: Likely the water-temperature sensor (NTC/thermistor) position. Measure resistance vs. temperature on the real board.

callouts.label: Through-hole joints of relay, fuse and mains terminals
callouts.note: MAINS POTENTIAL. Never probe with the unit plugged in.
